column1: For millennia, the coconut has been central to the lives of Polynesian and Asian peoples.
column2: 数千年来，椰子在波利尼西亚和亚洲各族人民的生活中一直占据重要地位。

column1: In the western world, on the other hand, coconuts have always been exotic and unusual, sometimes rare.
column2: 而对西方人来说，椰子一直是充满异域色彩的新奇事物，有时还十分罕见。
column4: on the other hand|另一方面

column1: The Italian merchant traveller Marco Polo apparently saw coconuts in South Asia in the late 13th century, and among the mid-14th-century travel writings of Sir John Mandeville there is mention of ‘great Notes of Ynde’ (great Nuts of India).
column2: 据说，意大利商人兼旅行家马可·波罗曾在13世纪末于南亚见到椰子。在约翰·曼德维尔爵士写于14世纪中期的游记里，也提到过“印度大坚果”。
column9: great Nuts of India|印度大坚果

column1: Today, images of palm-fringed tropical beaches are clichés in the west to sell holidays, chocolate bars, fizzy drinks and even romance.
column2: 如今在西方，椰树环绕的热带沙滩已是司空见惯的广告画面，常用来推销度假旅行、巧克力棒、汽水，甚至浪漫情调。
column5: clichés|n. 陈词滥调，俗套画面

column1: Typically, we envisage coconuts as brown cannonballs that, when opened, provide sweet white flesh.
column2: 我们通常把椰子想象成一颗棕色炮弹，打开后里面是甜甜的白色果肉。

column1: But we see only part of the fruit and none of the plant from which they come.
column2: 可是我们看到的只是果实的一部分，连生出它的那棵树都没看到。
column3: only part of|仅是……的一部分

column1: The coconut palm has a smooth, slender, grey trunk, up to 30 metres tall.
column2: 椰子树的树干光滑、细长，呈灰色，最高可达30米。

column1: This is an important source of timber for building houses, and is increasingly being used as a replacement for endangered hardwoods in the furniture construction industry.
column2: 树干是重要的建房木材来源。家具制造业也越来越多地用它来替代那些已受威胁的硬木。

column1: The trunk is surmounted by a rosette of leaves, each of which may be up to six metres long.
column2: 树干顶端长着一簇呈莲座状排列的叶片，每片最长可达六米。

column1: The leaves have hard veins in their centres which, in many parts of the world, are used as brushes after the green part of the leaf has been stripped away.
column2: 每片叶子中央有坚硬的叶脉。世界许多地方的人把绿色叶肉剥去，再用叶脉作刷子。

column1: Immature coconut flowers are tightly clustered together among the leaves at the top of the trunk.
column2: 尚未成熟的椰子花紧密地簇生在树冠的叶片之间。
column6: top of the trunk|树干顶端

column1: The flower stems may be tapped for their sap to produce a drink, and the sap can also be reduced by boiling to produce a type of sugar used for cooking.
column2: 人们可以割开花梗取汁，制成饮料；也可以熬煮浓缩汁液，制成一种烹饪用糖。
column6: reduced by boiling|通过熬煮浓缩

column1: Coconut palms produce as many as seventy fruits per year, weighing more than a kilogram each.
column2: 椰子树一年最多能结70个果实，每个都重逾一公斤。
column6: more than a kilogram|超过一公斤

column1: The wall of the fruit has three layers: a waterproof outer layer, a fibrous middle layer and a hard, inner layer.
column2: 果壁分为三层：防水的外层、富含纤维的中层，以及坚硬的内层。

column1: The thick fibrous middle layer produces coconut fibre, ‘coir’, which has numerous uses and is particularly important in manufacturing ropes.
column2: 厚厚的纤维中层能提供椰衣纤维，称为coir。它用途很多，制绳时尤其重要。

column1: The woody innermost layer, the shell, with its three prominent ‘eyes’, surrounds the seed.
column2: 木质的最内层就是椰壳，上面有三个醒目的“眼”，包裹着种子。

column1: An important product obtained from the shell is charcoal, which is widely used in various industries as well as in the home as a cooking fuel.
column2: 椰壳的一种重要产品是木炭。它广泛用于各行各业，在家庭中也用作炊事燃料。

column1: When broken in half, the shells are also used as bowls in many parts of Asia.
column2: 在亚洲许多地区，对半劈开的椰壳还会被用作碗。

column1: Inside the shell are the nutrients (endosperm) needed by the developing seed.
column2: 椰壳内是种子发育需要的营养物质，即胚乳。

column1: Initially, the endosperm is a sweetish liquid, coconut water, which is enjoyed as a drink, but also provides the hormones which encourage other plants to grow more rapidly and produce higher yields.
column2: 最初，胚乳是略带甜味的液体，也就是椰子水。它既是人们喜爱的饮料，又含有能促进其他植物生长、提高其产量的激素。

column1: As the fruit matures, the coconut water gradually solidifies to form the brilliant white, fat-rich, edible flesh or meat.
column2: 随着果实成熟，椰子水逐渐凝固，形成雪白、富含脂肪且可食用的椰肉。

column1: Dried coconut flesh, ‘copra’, is made into coconut oil and coconut milk, which are widely used in cooking in different parts of the world, as well as in cosmetics.
column2: 晒干的椰肉叫作copra，可制成椰子油和椰奶。两者在世界各地的烹饪中广泛使用，也用于化妆品。

column1: A derivative of coconut fat, glycerine, acquired strategic importance in a quite different sphere, as Alfred Nobel introduced the world to his nitroglycerine-based invention: dynamite.
column2: 椰子脂肪的一种衍生物甘油，在另一个截然不同的领域具有了战略意义。当时，阿尔弗雷德·诺贝尔向世界介绍了他以硝化甘油为基础的发明——达纳炸药。

column1: Their biology would appear to make coconuts the great maritime voyagers and coastal colonizers of the plant world.
column2: 椰子的生物学特性，似乎让它们成了植物界卓越的航海者和海岸开拓者。
column6: coastal colonizers|在海岸扎根拓展的物种

column1: The large, energy-rich fruits are able to float in water and tolerate salt, but cannot remain viable indefinitely; studies suggest after about 110 days at sea they are no longer able to germinate.
column2: 这些硕大、富含能量的果实能在水中漂浮，也耐盐，但活力无法无限期保持。研究显示，在海上漂流约110天后，椰子就不能再发芽了。

column1: Literally cast onto desert island shores, with little more than sand to grow in and exposed to the full glare of the tropical sun, coconut seeds are able to germinate and root.
column2: 椰子种子被海水冲上荒岛海岸，几乎只有沙子可供生长，还要经受热带烈日直晒，却能够萌发、生根。

column1: The air pocket in the seed, created as the endosperm solidifies, protects the embryo.
column2: 胚乳凝固时会在种子内部形成一个气腔，保护胚体。

column1: In addition, the fibrous fruit wall that helped it to float during the voyage stores moisture that can be taken up by the roots of the coconut seedling as it starts to grow.
column2: 此外，在海上漂流时帮助椰子浮起的纤维果壁还能储水；椰苗开始生长时，根就能吸收这些水分。

column1: There have been centuries of academic debate over the origins of the coconut.
column2: 关于椰子起源何处，学术界已经争论了数百年。

column1: There were no coconut palms in West Africa, the Caribbean or the east coast of the Americas before the voyages of the European explorers Vasco da Gama and Columbus in the late 15th and early 16th centuries.
column2: 在欧洲探险家瓦斯科·达·伽马和哥伦布于15世纪末至16世纪初出海远航以前，西非、加勒比地区和美洲东海岸都没有椰子树。
column5: east coast of the Americas|美洲东海岸

column1: 16th century trade and human migration patterns reveal that Arab traders and European sailors are likely to have moved coconuts from South and Southeast Asia to Africa and then across the Atlantic to the east coast of America.
column2: 16世纪的贸易和人口迁移路线显示，阿拉伯商人和欧洲水手很可能把椰子从南亚和东南亚运到非洲，再横渡大西洋，带到美洲东海岸。
column4: human migration patterns|人口迁移路线

column1: But the origin of coconuts discovered along the west coast of America by 16th century sailors has been the subject of centuries of discussion.
column2: 但是，16世纪水手们在美洲西海岸发现的椰子从何而来，却已争论了数百年。
column7: centuries of discussion|数百年的讨论

column1: Two diametrically opposed origins have been proposed: that they came from Asia, or that they were native to America.
column2: 关于椰子的来源，有两种截然相反的说法：一种认为椰子来自亚洲，另一种认为它原产于美洲。

column1: Both suggestions have problems.
column2: 两种说法各有难以解释之处。

column1: In Asia, there is a large degree of coconut diversity and evidence of millennia of human use — but there are no relatives growing in the wild.
column2: 亚洲椰子多样性很高，也有证据表明人类已利用它数千年，但那里却找不到野生的椰子近缘种。
column5: millennia of human use|数千年的人类利用

column1: In America, there are close coconut relatives, but no evidence that coconuts are indigenous.
column2: 美洲虽然有与椰子亲缘关系很近的植物，却没有证据能证明椰子是当地的原生物种。
column3: close coconut relatives|椰子的近缘种

column1: These problems have led to the intriguing suggestion that coconuts originated on coral islands in the Pacific and were dispersed from there.
column2: 这些疑点催生了一种耐人寻味的推测：椰子原产于太平洋珊瑚岛，后来才从那里传播到其他地方。
